flags.why: "more resting on 18th" doesn't say where. The bird earlier was "close to Isle of May", probably on the sea, which isn't a place `settled` covers. Either seen or settled fits.

"species of birds remaining on the island at this date" is a winter census of birds living on Rathlin, not birds resting at the station. It could be seen, or settled by analogy with "remained about the lighthouse".

The transcription puts the Tuskar entry under the heading "Linnet.", so "Linnet" copies the text exactly. The checker read a "Tits." heading on p. 83 of the print, so the transcription seems to have dropped that heading.
"four struck and two were killed at Butt of Lewis": under the rules, struck means hitting the lantern, so the killed birds are birds killed at the light.
No station appears in the chunk (a footnote) or its context (table rows only). The heading "Stevns Fyr" is outside both, and the rules say to use null in that case.

"night of 12th many round lantern, and night of 13th, 8 p.m. ...": whether "many" carries on to the 13th is a question of how far a count reaches. The extraction did carry round_lantern over, though, so "many" would be consistent.
"one was seen at lights": the round_lantern rule includes "at the lantern or light", and at_light is already true.
